thread.title: Apple: Not Priced For Buybacks Boost - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Apple: Not Priced For Buybacks Boost - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Despite a lot of noise regarding smartphone weakness, Apple ( AAPL ) estimates have remained robust. The tech giant is quickly shifting to a position not requiring iPhone sales expansion going forward and the estimates don't actually reflect a big buyback boost. The stock trades at a bargain at only 14.3x FY19 estimates that are far too low.
Image Source: Apple website
Mature Market The smartphone market has matured to where companies can't rely on meaningful growth going forward. The issue is even greater in the case of Apple with high-end phones and a focus on mature markets outside of Asia.
The market for smartphones hasn't grown much since 2014 while the competition from OEMs outside the U.S. has grown significantly in the last few years. In fact, most of the growth since 2010 has come from China OEMs that increasingly serve the demand from the untapped markets in Asia.
Source: Mary Meeker Internet Trends Report 2018
Citigroup analyst Jim Suva placed a $200 target on the stock due in part to a promising 2018 product lineup. His projection for single-digit unit growth would be a positive outcome though not one needed for a bullish thesis.
Source: CNBC
Analysts only forecast 4% revenue growth in FY19 that starts in October suggesting the market only forecasts limited growth from the iPhone. The bigger story with the stock remains the ability of Apple to grow sales and utilize massive cash flows to reduce the share count.
Oddly though, Loop Capital analyst Ananda Baruah raised the price target to $210 based in part on the launch of an LCD-based iPhone X that has a lower price point. A 5.8-inch OLED model with an ASP around $900 and a LCD 6.1-inch model with an ASP of $750 would help with unit sales while potentially pushing down the average ASP.
More units sold equates to more services and any actual revenue growth from iPhone sales in FY19 is more upside to the current estimates.
Financial Impact Apple will release FQ3 results on July 31, but the YTD numbers through March show how much the iPhone dominates the business. Even in the non-holiday March quarter, iPhone sales accounted for an incredible 62% of sales. The December holiday quarter was nearly 70% of sales.
Source: Apple FQ2'18 data summary
The key here is for Apple to at least maintain iPhone revenue levels as a gateway to the higher margin services. My previous research showcased how services provided for higher margins. Shifting the ASPs for the iPhone down slightly to increase units would provide long-term value from more consumers purchasing services like streaming music and an anticipated move into video.
Even with the $2 billion boost to services revenues in the March quarter and a 31% growth rate YoY, the sector boosted the revenue contribution by about 170 basis points to 15% of revenues. Where services really start shining are over the next couple of quarters due to recurring revenue streams offsetting traditional product sales weakness during the slow off-peak months.
During FQ3 and FQ4 last year, services accounted for 16% of revenues. Maintaining the recent 30% growth rate in services combined with a similar jump in the smaller Other Products group that includes the Apple Watch will help boost revenues even with stalling iPhone sales.
For FQ3, analysts forecast revenue growth for the whole company that amounts to roughly $6.9 billion in additional revenue. Services will account for ~32% of additional revenue with a 30% annualized growth rate maintained.
Other products could provide another ~12% of the additional revenue leaving only roughly half of the growth coming from traditional hardware products like the iPhone that is still cycling through the addition of the high-end iPhone X this year.
Next year though, Apple won't see the benefit from the new iPhone X. As the FQ3 table shows, the Services and Other Products divisions would together produce growth that propels total company growth nearly 7%.
Any actual growth from the iPhone would propel total revenue far above the 4% forecast by analysts.
EPS Estimates - Buybacks Boost The point on the above analysis is that Apple has the ability to grow revenues based on growth from Services. The recently announced $100 billion share buyback is a further boost to EPS.
At the current market cap of $925 billion, the approved buyback would repurchase ~11% of the outstanding shares. Based on the $11.50 analyst EPS estimate for FY18, an 11% share reduction would add about $1.27 per share to EPS estimates.
AAPL EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts Another key point is that the reduction of the tax rate from over 25% for the December quarter last year to 15% this year automatically adds ~$0.56 to the FY19 estimate. So if Apple leverages up 4% revenue growth into 8% EPS growth based on the shift to higher margin services and using a $12.06 EPS starting point, nearly $1 of the EPS gain is related to pure improvements in the business.
The combination suggests analysts are only factoring in a $0.10 EPS boost next year due to a lower share count. Naturally, analysts are factoring in part of the EPS boost from the large $100 billion buyback to the $11.50 number for FY18, but the program was only announced in April with the FQ2 report.
The odd part of the EPS estimates is that Apple has traditionally reduced shares at a fast clip. The company has averaged in the annualized range of about 5% share reductions for years now.
AAPL Average Diluted Shares Outstanding (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts Taking a $12 normalized EPS level in FY19 due to taxes, a 5% share reduction boosts EPS by $0.60. The accelerated buyback could provide an even bigger boost than only 5%. A legitimate EPS target for FY19 has to start at $13.50 and move higher.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that no matter how one slices it, Apple is positioned to beat the current EPS targets for FY19. Higher margin services revenues should leverage up revenue growth while analyst projections of solid iPhone sales should lead to a revenue beat.
The combination is higher revenues and margins along with left over tax benefits leading to the majority of the projected EPS growth next year. The end result is that a cheaper stock gets even cheaper with estimates that actually factors in legitimate share reduction in FY19.
Apple only trades at 13.8x my baseline estimate of $13.50 per share for FY19. Ex-cash, the stock is even cheaper though the smaller net cash position with the market cap approaching $1 trillion will lessen the value in making that calculation.
Disclosure: I am/we are long aapl, AAPL.
